# image-scout

**Give your agent eyes.** Find a real photograph on the public web, download it, and prove
it is a r
eal image before the rest of your workflow touches it.

`image-scout` is a DeepSeek Harness plugin
that bundles one agent skill and one zero-dependency Node

.js CLI. It answers the question
agents are bad at: *is this URL actually a photo, and can I trust i

CLI. It answers the question
agents are bad at: *is this URL actually a photo, and can I trust it?*
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What it does
| Command | What it guarantees |
| `search` | Queries the Wikimedia Commons or Openverse API; returns title, pixel size, licence, aut
hor, file page and direct image URL | | `list` | Fetches a page and extracts ``, `srcset` and `

og:image` candidates, with the full-size URL when it can derive it |
| `download` | Downloads one UR
L, **refuses URLs that are not on the declared page**, then checks magic bytes, dimensions and file

size before writing |
| `verify` | Re-checks any file on disk with the same three checks |
No daemon, no cache directory, no config file, no API key, no npm dependencies.

## Why not just fetch the URL?

Because "downloaded" is not the same as "got an image". A consent wall, a 429 page, a
hotlink-protec

tion redirect and a 250 px thumbnail all return HTTP 200. `download`
therefore checks, in order:

1. **Provenance** — the URL must appear on the page you named (query strings and Wikimedia
thumb siz

es are normalised, so the full-size URL of a listed thumb is accepted).
2. **Magic bytes** — JPEG, P

NG, GIF or WEBP signature; an HTML error page never passes.
3. **Dimensions** — parsed from the head

er (`SOF` for JPEG, `IHDR` for PNG, the frame header
for GIF/WEBP) without decoding the pixels.
4. *

*Size floor** — rejects tracking pixels and placeholders below `--min-bytes` (2 KB default).
5. **At

omic write** — temp file + rename, so an interrupted download cannot leave a truncated
image that la

emp file + rename, so an interrupted download cannot leave a truncated
image that later looks valid.
Anything else exits non-zero and writes nothing.
## Sources and licences
| Source | How | Notes |
| **Wikimedia Commons** | `--source wikimedia` (default) | Highest resolution, licence + author in t

he API response, mostly CC |
| **Openverse** | `--source openverse` | Aggregates Flickr and others;

check for `NC` (no commercial) and `ND` (no derivatives) |
| **Any page** | `list` + `download --pag
e-url` | Works on gallery and article pages; often only a thumbnail is embedded |

Every download writes `<file>.json` with the source URL, licence (when passed with
`--license`), dim

ensions and timestamp. Keep it — that is your attribution record. The
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- Node.js 22.19+ or 24+ (the CLI uses `parseArgs`, `fetch`-free `http`-level proxy support
and nativ

e ESM).
- Outbound HTTPS to `commons.wikimedia.org`, `upload.wikimedia.org` and (optionally)
`api.op

enverse.org`. Behind a proxy, set `HTTPS_PROXY` or pass `--proxy`.
- No dependencies. `npm install`
installs nothing, because there is nothing to install.
